name: Smith Machine Sissy Squat
description: A sissy squat variation performed with the Smith machine bar resting across the front of the thighs, with heels elevated on a plate or wedge. The machine guides the movement and reduces balance demand, allowing heavy quad isolation with the knees traveling far forward — a position that maximally stretches and loads the rectus femoris and vastus lateralis.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing away from the Smith machine with the bar set at approximately thigh height. Place heels on a 25lb plate. Bar rests lightly across upper thighs.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the Smith bar at thigh height. Place a 25lb plate flat behind the foot position for heel elevation. Duck under the bar and position it across the upper thighs.
steps: Step 1: Lean back slightly with a rigid torso, engaging the quads.
Step 2: Allow the knees to travel forward over and past the toes while your hips drop toward the floor.
Step 3: Lower until a strong quad stretch is felt, or as far as comfortable knee health allows.
Step 4: Reverse the motion by driving the knees back and straightening to the upright position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent. Exhale during the return to upright.
common_mistakes: Collapsing the lower back — maintain a rigid torso throughout
Using excessive range before the tendons have adapted
safety_considerations: Avoid if you have patellar tendinopathy or significant knee pain
Progress depth gradually over several weeks
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lower until a strong quad stretch is felt. The knees travel well past the toes — this is intentional for this exercise.
